page: Amazon Web Services r8g.12xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by custom 64-bit Arm-based AWS Graviton processors. Utilizing the Neoverse-V2 core architecture, the instance provides 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, with no hyperthreading. It features 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, has a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps, and does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data highlights the instance's strong memory subsystem and multi-core execution capabilities. The r8g.12xlarge achieves top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, registering 404.36 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 201.11 GB/sec for large-block write operations. This memory efficiency is reflected in its top-tier Passmark memory score and database operations score. Multi-core compute performance is also strong, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 23531.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 81875.49. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier, as shown by its Geekbench single-core score of 1894.0 and stress-ng single-core CPU performance of 1706.6.

Given its high memory density and strong multi-core throughput, the r8g.12xlarge is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale database operations, caching layers, and memory-bound data processing. The instance demonstrates top-tier static web serving throughput at 103.71 GB/sec and strong performance in Redis SET operations, processing 100.01 million operations per second. While it handles medium and large LLM text generation tasks with strong relative efficiency, its lack of local storage and GPU accelerators makes it less suitable for heavy GPU-bound deep learning training. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the custom Arm64 architecture delivers high resource density and memory bandwidth per unit of compute, offering a favorable performance-to-resource profile for enterprise database and web serving environments.
